summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, COPD, diastolic heart failure, and diabetes was admitted with acute respiratory distress and generalized weakness. She was initially intubated due to inability to protect her airway and treated in the ICU for hypercarbic respiratory failure, sepsis from Klebsiella pneumonia, acute kidney injury, and acute on chronic heart failure. She was weaned off the ventilator, extubated, and transferred to the medical floor. Her infections resolved with antibiotics, fluid status improved with diuresis, and kidney function normalized. Despite recommendations, she refused rehabilitation and certain respiratory supports. Goals of care were discussed, and she agreed to palliative care follow-up at home. She was discharged to home with services on optimized medical therapy.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
